LESSON: HOLDING TOOLS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Tools and Production
Topic 4.1: Holding Tools
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Holding Tools, part of Tools and Production in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How are holding tools used in the immediate environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Holding Tools together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: learner develops observing/listening and signing/speaking skills when learners practise

how to fingerspell and sign terms related to holding tools.

• Learning to Learn: learner reflects on own work when demonstrating safe use of holding tools when performing different

types of tasks.

• Digital Literacy: learner develops digital skills when using digital devices and print media to search for information or

captioned videos on care for holding tools.

36

Values:
• Unity: learner cooperates with others when discussing on the safe use of holding tools.

• Responsibility: learner exercises accountability as they clean and safely store holding tools.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Personal Safety and Security: learner demonstrates basic safety habits as they safely use holding tools to perform tasks.

• Disaster Risk Reduction: learner appreciates the need to clean and safely store holding tools.

Link to other subjects:

Agriculture and Nutrition: learner enhances the knowledge on use of farm tools during demonstration on the safe use of

holding tools when performing different types of tasks.

Suggested learning resources

• Pliers, Clamps, spanners, vice, Tongs, clips among others

• Career brochures, career magazines

• Digital devices such as; computer, laptop, smart phone, tablets among others
